page: Microsoft Azure L32aos_v4 is a storage and memory-optimized server instance powered by the AMD EPYC 9V74 processor. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it features 32 dedicated vCPUs derived from 16 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The system operates at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz and is equipped with 256.0 GB of system memory, yielding 8.0 GB of RAM per core. A key hardware feature is the inclusion of 23,038 GB of local storage, and the instance is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core and multi-core capabilities. The server achieves top-tier performance in Geekbench single-core and multi-core tests, alongside strong results in image processing, text processing, and Passmark CPU encryption. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression also ranks in the top 25% at 196.26 GB/sec. Conversely, multi-core stress-ng performance, memory bandwidth, and Redis SET operations fall within the average range. LLM inference speeds are strong for small models but drop to average tiers for medium and large models.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the L32aos_v4 offers high local storage density and a balanced memory-to-vCPU ratio, making it highly resource-dense for data-intensive applications without requiring external storage attachments. However, the lack of dedicated GPU hardware limits its utility for heavy deep learning training, and memory bandwidth remains average. This hardware profile is optimal for large-scale databases, data warehousing, heavy text and image processing pipelines, and memory-intensive enterprise workloads.
